title: The Rocky Road from Aggregate to Per Share Value: Anthropic's IPO update
gist: Damodaran updates his Anthropic IPO valuation to ~$1.35T equity (down from $1.475T) on higher post-midterm data-center costs, larger regulatory margin drag and smaller $60B proceeds, and argues the option-adjusted value of ~$76/share is the right per-share number versus the $83 offer. He uses Anthropic's messy capital structure (801M IPO shares, 1,026M restricted, 1,774M deep-ITM options, single founder voting share) to argue share count is the unstandardized 'Wild West' of valuation and market-cap reporting.

insights.claim: Aswath Damodaran cut his Anthropic aggregate equity value from $1.475 trillion (Nov 2, 2026) to about $1.352 trillion ($1,351,556 million) after the updated prospectus, with the drop mostly from higher compute costs and regulatory drag.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Anchor for Anthropic post-IPO fair value: roughly $1.35T equity in Damodaran's intrinsic model.
insights.quote: The resulting aggregated equity value is $1,351,556 million, with the drop in estimated value mostly a result of the updated compute costs and regulatory drag.
insights.locator: To arrive at the value per share

insights.claim: Damodaran treats the 2026 US midterm election outcome as making data centers more expensive to build, cutting Anthropic's sales-to-invested-capital ratio for the first five years from $3 to $2.75, which raises reinvestment needs and lowers cash flows.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Political shift raises AI capex intensity; watch data-center permitting/cost data as a valuation input for AI labs and hyperscalers.
insights.quote: assume that building data centers will become more expensive (captured by lowering the sales Anthropic will get per dollar of capital invested in the first five years from $3 to $2.75
insights.locator: I do not want to overreact

insights.claim: Anticipating stricter AI regulation from a new Congress, Damodaran raised the regulatory drag on Anthropic's margins from 5% to 6%, lowering its target operating margin to 26.5%.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: AI regulation risk is now an explicit margin haircut in valuations of AI model companies.
insights.quote: the drag on margins will get larger, from 5% to 6%, lowering the target margin to 26.5%
insights.locator: It is unclear whether and how

insights.claim: Anthropic's expected IPO cash proceeds were revised down from a rumored $100 billion to about $60 billion (801 million new shares at an expected $74), reducing post-IPO equity value by $40 billion.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Smaller raise than rumored means less cash cushion on the balance sheet post-IPO.
insights.locator: I adjusted the cash proceeds down

insights.claim: Adding Q3 2026 numbers to Anthropic's trailing base year had a muted valuation effect because the slowdown in annualized revenue run rate in the third quarter was already known and priced into the earlier story.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Q3 run-rate deceleration is not new information for valuation; don't overreact to it.
insights.quote: while there was a slowing down in the annualized revenue run rate in the third quarter, that was already known
insights.locator: I updated the base year numbers

insights.claim: Anthropic recorded a $74 billion one-time, non-cash charge to 2026 earnings from accounting for the surge in value of convertible-bond conversion options as its private-market pricing rose.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Reported 2026 GAAP earnings are distorted by a $74B non-cash charge; adjust before using P/E.
insights.quote: it is the accounting for the surge in the value of the conversion option, as its pricing increased in private markets, that led to the $74 billion one-time and non-cash charge to earnings in 2026
insights.locator: Conclusion

insights.claim: Damodaran's Anthropic per-share value ranges from $76.46 (fully diluted) to $90.86 (primary shares), but he uses the option-adjusted value of about $76 per share as his estimate.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: With the IPO priced at $83, Damodaran's preferred intrinsic value (~$76) implies the offer is roughly 9% above fair value before any first-day pop.
insights.quote: the value that I would use is the option adjusted value per share of $76.

insights.claim: Anthropic's IPO offer price was set at $83 per share, above the earlier expected range of $70-78, and Damodaran notes the higher offer price slightly lowers value per share under all his calculations.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Offer priced above intrinsic estimate; the relevant comparison is the opening trade price.
insights.quote: the news story reported that the offer price has been set at $83/share
insights.locator: Note that while there is a range

insights.claim: Damodaran argues the real test of Anthropic's valuation is not the offer price but the price at which the stock opens trading on its first day.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Compare first-day open versus ~$76 intrinsic to judge over/undervaluation.
insights.quote: the real comparison should be to the price that Anthropic will open trading at tomorrow

themes.theme: Anthropic share count and dilution details

insights.claim: Anthropic's share count ranges from 14,875.18 million (shares outstanding only) to 17,676.18 million fully diluted, a ~19% gap that makes per-share value swing widely depending on the count used.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Market-cap and per-share figures for Anthropic will differ materially across data providers depending on dilution treatment.
insights.locator: With those caveats in place

insights.claim: Anthropic's IPO issues 801 million new class A shares, and there are 1,026 million restricted shares under four-year vesting with none yet vested.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Large unvested restricted stock pool is a future dilution and supply overhang.

insights.claim: Anthropic has 1,774 million employee options outstanding with a $2.91 strike, deep in the money against a $70-78 expected offer, 1,082 million already vested, and about eight years of remaining life (small time premium).
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Over a billion vested deep-ITM options can become sellable supply after lockups.

insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Donation-plan and convertible-conversion shares add to effective float and dilution beyond the headline count.

themes.theme: Founder share governance and expropriation risk

insights.claim: Anthropic's voting rights sit in a single founder share (class T / trust holders with 50.01% of votes in perpetuity), so Damodaran declined to value share classes separately.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Public Class A holders get economic exposure with effectively no control.
insights.quote: the voting rights reside in a single share owned by the founders
insights.locator: Note that I have studiously avoided

insights.claim: Damodaran compares Anthropic's founder share to the golden shares governments kept in privatized utilities in the 1980s-1990s, but notes the founder share is far more powerful because golden shares only veto major decisions, not day-to-day operations.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Concentrated single-share control is an unusual governance risk to price.
insights.quote: Anthropic's founder share is far more powerful, and I do think that there is a danger in loading up this much power in a single share.
insights.locator: Note that I have studiously avoided

insights.claim: Damodaran warns that concentrating control in one founder share creates a tail risk that an activist regulator, after an AI accident, could cite public safety to expropriate that share and turn Anthropic into a government-controlled utility.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Unusual nationalization-style tail risk for AI labs with concentrated control structures; monitor AI-safety incidents and regulatory posture.

themes.theme: Share count methods in intrinsic valuation

insights.claim: Damodaran argues the absence of standardization has made share count the 'Wild West' of investing, because multiple share classes and stock-based compensation complicate the move from aggregate to per-share value.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Per-share valuations and market caps of SBC-heavy firms deserve independent verification.
insights.quote: the absence of standardization has made share count the Wild West in investing
insights.locator: I valued Anthropic in a post

insights.claim: Using the primary share count overstates value per share for firms with restricted stock and options, while the fully diluted count understates it by counting out-of-the-money options and ignoring exercise proceeds.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Both the conservative fully diluted and the headline primary per-share numbers are biased; neither should anchor decisions.
insights.locator: Share Count in Intrinsic Valuation

insights.claim: The treasury stock approach adds in-the-money option exercise proceeds to equity value but ignores options' time premium, so it undervalues options and produces a per-share value that is too high.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Treasury stock method common in sell-side models systematically overstates per-share value.
insights.locator: The Refined Bludgeon

insights.claim: Damodaran's preferred method values all employee options (in and out of the money) with an option pricing model, subtracts that from aggregate equity value, and divides by primary plus restricted shares to get the option-adjusted value per share.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Use option-adjusted value per share for SBC-heavy growth firms; disclosure of strike and maturity makes it feasible for US companies.
insights.quote: the right approach in valuation is to estimate the value of options, using an option pricing model) and then subtract that value from aggregate equity value
insights.locator: The Scalpel

insights.claim: Young firms that rely heavily on stock-based compensation because they lack cash have the largest gaps between primary and fully diluted share counts, making share-count choice most consequential there.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Scrutinize footnotes on restricted stock, options and convertibles for early-lifecycle companies.
insights.locator: For some older and more mature

insights.claim: Financial data services report differing market capitalizations for the same high-profile companies at the same time because they use different share counts, and the divergence widens for young, high-growth firms with large SBC overhangs.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: EV multiples and P/E ratios for the same company can differ across data vendors; check share-count basis before comparing.
insights.locator: Almost every financial data news service

insights.claim: Using the same dilution convention across a peer group does not make multiples comparable, because companies differ widely in their use of restricted stock and options.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Relative valuation screens across SBC-heavy peers can be misleading.
insights.locator: If you are comparing across companies

insights.claim: Damodaran proposes an option-adjusted market capitalization (share price times primary plus restricted shares, plus the value of employee and conversion options) and says no data service he knows of uses it.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Option-adjusted market cap enables apples-to-apples comparison across firms with different option overhangs.
insights.locator: So what is the correct market capitalization

insights.claim: Damodaran expects data services to report inconsistent market capitalizations for Anthropic once it lists, and says both the purely primary-share estimate (too high) and the fully diluted estimate (too low) will be off versus the correct option-adjusted figure.
insights.speaker: Aswath Damodaran
insights.so_what: Expect wide dispersion in reported Anthropic market cap and multiples post-listing; normalize before ranking it vs peers.
insights.locator: Once Anthropic goes public tomorrow
